title: JFK - Lone Gunman or Conspiracy
style: cinematic documentary still, 1960s period setting, 35mm film grain, muted desaturated colour, moody dramatic lighting
ambience: Low, tense ambient atmosphere with faint room tone, no music.

segments.text: On the twenty second of November, nineteen sixty three, President Kennedy was shot in Dallas. Officially, one man acted alone. But does that story really hold together?
segments.shot: A wide view of Dealey Plaza in Dallas in 1963, an empty sunlit street curving past grassy lawns and a red brick building, no people.

segments.text: The Warren Commission concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald fired three shots from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository, overlooking Dealey Plaza.
segments.shot: A low angle of a seven storey red brick 1960s warehouse building, slowly drifting up towards an open corner window on the sixth floor, overcast sky, no people.

segments.text: Critics seized on the so-called magic bullet: a single round that, officially, wounded both the President and Governor Connally. Sceptics doubt any bullet could do that.
segments.shot: A close-up of a single copper bullet in a small clear evidence bag lying on typed 1960s report pages, a brass magnifying glass beside it, lit by a desk lamp in a dark office.

segments.text: Then there's the grassy knoll. A number of witnesses insisted they heard shots from behind the wooden fence there, not from the Depository at all.
segments.shot: A grassy slope topped by a weathered wooden picket fence and trees, early morning light with drifting mist, empty and silent.

segments.text: And in nineteen seventy nine, a congressional committee concluded Kennedy was probably killed as the result of a conspiracy, though its key acoustic evidence was later disputed.
segments.shot: An empty 1970s congressional hearing room with long wooden desks, microphones and stacks of documents, dust floating in shafts of window light.

segments.text: Oswald himself never stood trial. Two days later, he was shot dead by Jack Ruby, live on television, taking his answers with him.
segments.shot: A vintage 1960s television set glowing in a dim living room, its screen showing grainy black and white static, a cup of coffee on the side table, no people.

segments.text: Thousands of files have since been released, yet the debate goes on. So, lone gunman, or something more? Look at the evidence, and decide for yourself.
segments.shot: Stacks of old declassified government folders and boxes in a dim archive, papers spilling out, a single lamp.
